nations.name: MOWA Band of Choctaw Indians
nations.lands: Mobile and Washington Counties in southwestern Alabama, near the Mobile and Tombigbee Rivers

facts.text: The Tribe's introduction places its communities in Mobile and Washington Counties in southwestern Alabama.
facts.evidence: Choctaw Indians of Mobile and Washington Counties

facts.text: Its history explains MOWA as a name drawn from Mobile and Washington Counties.

source.title: We Are Choctaw: A Historical Account of Tradition and Progress - MOWA Band of Choctaw Indians

facts.evidence: draw their name from the two counties they straddle

facts.text: The Tribe's land history describes logging as both a source of jobs and displacement for families.

source.title: Land & Timber Industry - MOWA Band of Choctaw Indians

facts.evidence: This displaced families, but it also provided jobs.

facts.text: Its history dates an effort to obtain federal aid for Alabama Choctaw schools to 1934.

source.title: Social Barriers - MOWA Band of Choctaw Indians

facts.evidence: Federal Aid Sought for Alabama Choctaw Schools (1934)
